title: What an ORM does
idea: An ORM (object-relational mapper) lets you query a database with JavaScript functions. It builds the SQL and returns rows as plain objects.

analogy.text: A translator at a meeting. You speak JavaScript, the translator speaks SQL to the database, then turns the reply back into JavaScript.
analogy.breaks: A translator can mistranslate; the SQL an ORM sends is yours to check.

points: You describe each table once in JavaScript, as an object such as `books`.
Methods such as `select`, `from` and `where` build the SQL text for you.
Values travel apart from the SQL as parameters, so input cannot rewrite the query.
Trade-off: you learn another API, and slow queries still need SQL knowledge.

messages.label: select().from().where()
messages.note: You describe the query with function calls. Nothing is sent until you `await` it.

messages.label: select … where year > $1
messages.note: Drizzle builds the SQL text. The value 1970 travels apart from it, as `$1`.

messages.label: 2 rows
messages.note: Postgres runs the SQL and returns the matching rows.

messages.label: array of objects
messages.note: Drizzle turns each row into a plain object, such as `{ title: 'Neuromancer' }`.

code.title: Raw SQL and Drizzle
code.caption: The same question asked twice: with a SQL string, then with Drizzle. Step through it, then press Run.

walk.text: `pg` is the driver that talks to Postgres. Drizzle builds queries on top of it.
The table, described as a JavaScript object. Three lessons on, you write this for the Book Store.
Raw SQL creates and fills the table. This is setup, not the lesson.
Without an ORM: you write the SQL and pass the value as `$1`.
With Drizzle: the same query as function calls. Nothing is sent yet.
`toSQL()` shows the SQL Drizzle will send. Compare it with the raw string.
`await` sends the query and returns plain objects. Closing the pool lets the script exit.

pitfalls: Do not skip SQL: when a query is slow, read the SQL the ORM sends.
An ORM does not make queries fast; indexes and query shape still matter.
Build queries with the ORM's methods; do not paste user input into SQL strings.

quiz.why: Drizzle sends the value as a parameter, apart from the SQL text, so it stays plain data.

takeaway: An ORM writes the SQL for you; you still own what it sends.
